title.narrative: COVAX facility to ensure global access to COVID-19 vaccines though the Advance Market Commitment (AMC) 2022

description.narrative:
The COVAX facility has 191 participating countries. This includes 99 self-financing participants and 92 AMC-eligible countries (middle- and low-income countries). For the self-financing countries, COVAX provides additional safety by supplementing possibilities to secure vaccines and because support to global vaccine provision reduces risks of virus mutations that represent a global risk. For the 92 AMC-eligible countries, COVAX AMC represents one of few opportunities to access COVID-19 vaccines. This contribution is core support to COVAX AMC especially targeting provision of vaccines to Africa.
The key strategic goals for Gavi’s COVID-19 response in 2023 is based on WHO’s base case scenario. To that end, COVAX aims to continue supporting AMC participants to meet their ambitions, with a particular emphasis on expanding protection for higher-risk populations and in line with the evolving product and policy landscape. A first high-level vaccine forecast for 2023 and beyond has been developed based on demand modelling and scenario planning and looks at three segments: - 1) expansion of primary and first booster coverage in line with national targets; - 2) introduction of additional booster campaigns for higher priority use groups; and - 3) limited continued provision of paediatric doses for high-risk children aged 6-11 years.
The contribution of DKK 75 million to COVAX will help achieve the above-mentioned targets and complement Denmark’s core support to Gavi. The Danish COVAX contribution is in line with the Danish development strategy and the goal of securing access to healthcare services as well as the policy to leave-no-one behind.
1.7 million deaths are estimated to have been averted through COVAX-supported COVID-19 vaccines across Gavi COVAX AMC participants up to June 2022, with approximately 75% of low-income countries’ supply of COVID-19 vaccines coming through COVAX.
Low-income countries including many countries in Sub- Saharan Africa do not have the means to secure COVID-19 vaccines and therefore risk that the pandemic will continue to cause loss of lives, over-burden health sectors and have socio-economic consequences including increased poverty and inequality.
Supporting provision of COVID-19 vaccines in low- and middle-income countries, especially in Africa, therefore contributes to improved health and immunisation, while also preventing that progress across sustainable development goals is lost because of the pandemic.
